reviewed_by: Delegated coding agent static review against live Binary Ninja 6.0.10601 MCP (retail PE view_1), radare2 6.2.0 CFG and angr 10.0.4.post1 CFGFast on retail igi.exe; candidate source read from this worktree. No game process was executed and no runtime behavior is claimed.
review_basis: Retail 0x004B8C60 was re-disassembled, re-decompiled and re-CFG'd through the live Binary Ninja view, independently recovered with radare2 6.2.0 and angr 10.0.4.post1 CFGFast. The candidate is scripts/GameNatives/script/004B8C60-_Script_SetWarningLevel.cpp at sha256 39215cd8c63f72a83423fb43b4bcf1df44021ace2bb5e14b3065aaf52b5340f5 (recorded implementation.signature: int32_t _Script_SetWarningLevel(int32_t param_1, float param_2);). The evidence artifact digests are bound in this review.

retail_function.name: _Script_SetWarningLevel
retail_function.summary: Single block 0x4B8C60-0x4B8CB0: call 0x4B8A20 (Script_EvalArgInt, arg2, 0), feed the result to 0x4B8970 (Sys_ExecuteBytecode_23), then rep-movsd a 24-byte record {0,?,0,0,&g_script_ret_type,?} from [E-0xC] to the result buffer read from [E+0x10], and return [E+0x10]. The QVM frame pointer is read from [E+0xc].

candidate_function.summary: Script_SetWarningLevel(int context, float arg2) performs the same two calls and the same 24-byte record copy, but declares `context` at [E+4] and `arg2` at [E+8].

divergences: QVM frame slot: retail reads [E+0xc], the candidate's second parameter is at [E+8].
Result buffer: retail returns/writes [E+0x10], the candidate's first parameter is [E+4].
The candidate returns the wrong word (its context slot instead of the [E+0x10] buffer).
candidate_comparison.statement: Divergences are listed above; by contract they keep the record at TRANSCRIBED or lower.

checks.name: function_identity
checks.detail: Retail entry 0x004B8C60 is recovered by all three tools; the address-bound implementation is scripts/GameNatives/script/004B8C60-_Script_SetWarningLevel.cpp (sha256 39215cd8c63f72a83423fb43b4bcf1df44021ace2bb5e14b3065aaf52b5340f5). Single block 0x4B8C60-0x4B8CB0: call 0x4B8A20 (Script_EvalArgInt, arg2, 0), feed the result to 0x4B8970 (Sys_ExecuteBytecode_23), then rep-movsd a 24-byte record {0,?,0,0,&g_script_ret_type,?} from [E-0xC] to the result buffer read from [E+0x10], and return [E+0x10]. The QVM frame pointer is read from [E+0xc]. Candidate: Script_SetWarningLevel(int context, float arg2) performs the same two calls and the same 24-byte record copy, but declares `context` at [E+4] and `arg2` at [E+8].

checks.name: abi_and_signature
checks.detail: BN models the frame word at [E+0xc] (`int32_t(int32_t arg1, float arg2 @ 0xc)`) and the result buffer at [E+0x10]. The candidate declares `(int context, float arg2)`, i.e. [E+4] and [E+8], so both QVM words are read from the wrong slots.

checks.name: argument_mapping
checks.detail: Retail reads the QVM frame from [E+0xc] and writes the result to [E+0x10]; the candidate's context/arg2 occupy [E+4] and [E+8]. The argument layout is shifted by two words.

checks.name: control_flow_shape
checks.detail: Binary Ninja and radare2 agree on 1 blocks / 0 edges (similarity 1.000); angr CFGFast recovers 5 blocks with has_unresolved_jumps=false. The angr block-count difference is a granularity artifact of CFGFast splitting at call returns / rep movsd; the BN and radare2 block and edge tables are identical.

checks.name: calls_and_side_effects
checks.detail: Retail calls 0x4B8A20 then 0x4B8970; the candidate calls the same addresses under the names Script_GetArg / Sys_ExecuteBytecode_23 (Project OpenIGI binds Script_GetArg to 0x004B8A20 in engine/src/retail/terrain).

checks.name: constants_and_scaling
checks.detail: The 24-byte record, the 0x18 count and the g_script_ret_type pointer match.

checks.name: memory_layout_and_access
checks.detail: The 24-byte stack record layout and its copy to the result buffer match retail.

checks.name: return_and_error_paths
checks.detail: Retail returns the result-buffer pointer read from [E+0x10]; the candidate returns its `context` parameter ([E+4]), so the returned pointer is wrong.

signature_comparison.rationale: Binary Ninja reports "int32_t(int32_t arg1, float arg2 @ 0xc)" at 0x004B8C60; radare2 recovers "fcn.004b8c60 (int32_t arg_30h, int32_t arg_24h);". Both tools place the entry at 0x004B8C60 and agree on the stack/register word count and cleanup; the difference is the level of type/argument-name detail, not the call frame. Candidate declaration: int32_t _Script_SetWarningLevel(int32_t param_1, float param_2);. The candidate declaration is separately recorded as divergent below and does not satisfy the retail ABI.

limitations: No game process was executed; this review is static (live Binary Ninja, radare2 CFG, angr CFGFast) plus the candidate source.
The candidate defines Script_SetWarningLevel while the catalog name carries a leading underscore (_Script_SetWarningLevel).
